text:
sam: Heads-up — billing dashboard shows a large hosted GPU charge spike overnight that doesn't match our committed reservation usage. Looks like burst credits were not applied to a chunk of traffic.

jess: Ugh. Which region and timeframe?

sam: ap-southeast-1, ~00:30-03:10 UTC. Hosted requests/sec jumped ~4x for a 40-minute tail. Invoice line: "on-demand GPU hours". Expected to be covered by committed pool.

kai: ops-bot alert earlier: "reserved-capacity-utilization >= 95%" then we saw autoscale open extra nodes. Could be routing to on-demand after pool exhaustion.

ops-bot: Alert: reserved-pool-ap-southeast-1 usage 98% (2026-03-18T00:45Z). Autoscale action: added 4 on-demand instances.

mike: Can you paste the query you used for the invoice correlation? I'll crosscheck with cloud billing export.

sam: pasted the quick gcloud/bq query I used:

```
SELECT sku.description, SUM(cost) as cost, TIMESTAMP_TRUNC(usage_start_time, HOUR) as hr
FROM `company_billing.gcp_export.gcp_billing_export_v1`
WHERE project.id = 'redwood-hosted' AND sku.id LIKE '%GPU%'
AND usage_start_time BETWEEN '2026-03-18T00:00:00Z' AND '2026-03-18T04:00:00Z'
GROUP BY sku.description, hr
ORDER BY hr;
```

jess: Nice. I see two hypotheses: 1) reserved pool exhausted and routing policy fell back to on-demand, 2) credit reconciliation bug where reserved hours weren't consumed from committed bucket.

kai: Our routing policy says: prefer reserved pool, fallback to on-demand only if capacity < request. But there's also a burst-crediting config that can consume reserved quotas across customer-tenants; might be a race condition.

mike: I ran the billing export join with our scheduling logs. Evidence: 00:48-01:30 a lot of requests got scheduled onto nodes labeled "on-demand-autoscale-" with instance.metadata.pool=ondemand. Cost lines line up. So fallback path triggered.

sam: Did the pool actually have free slots? The pool metrics show 2 free slots at 00:45, then suddenly a bunch of short-lived allocations.

kai: That matches a scheduling spike where we had small instances freed but by the time the job landed, our placement filter couldn't place due to GPU memory fragmentation (KV cache sticky). So scheduler opened on-demand nodes.

jess: Action items: 1) mike to attach billing export slices to ticket, 2) kai to check scheduler logs + placement failure reasons, 3) sam to quantify estimated cost delta and propose short-term mitigations (throttle burst, extend reserved capacity).

mike: Filed ticket INFRA-6821 with billing export samples and invoice references. Attaching sample rows: sku: NVIDIA-A100, cost $19.2/hr, 00:50-01:20 window.

kai: Found placement failures in scheduler logs: "insufficient contiguous GPU mem" and "kv-cache-held-by-ephemeral" at 00:46:12 -> 00:49:02. Looks like many cache pins from long-running hosted sessions prevented co-location.

sam: Estimated incremental cost for that window: ~$8.5k. Will present delta to finance.

jess: Short-term mitigation: enable soft-eviction on low-priority KV caches for hosted workloads in ap-southeast-1 for the next 48h, and raise reserved pool threshold from 90% to 95% to delay fallback. Any objections?

mike: +1 for soft-eviction. Need a rollback plan if tail latency regresses. I'll prepare metrics dashboard watchers.

kai: I'll implement a temporary scheduler change: prefer packing by GPU memory fragmentation score and allow co-tenancy relax for ephemeral tasks. Rolling change with canary in ap-southeast-1 only.

sam: I'll draft the finance message and estimate commit bump cost vs forecasted usage.

jess: We'll reconvene post-canary. Assign owners: mike (billing attach + dashboard), kai (scheduler patch + logs), sam (cost estimate + finance note).

ops-bot: Deployment started: scheduler-packing-tweak v2 -> canary ap-southeast-1. CI build 2026.03.18-07.

mike: Noting follow-up: check that committed pool metering increments align with scheduler attribution tag (pool_id) — we saw some on-demand lines without pool_id tags which blocks automatic reconciliation.

sam: Good catch. If pool attribution isn't tagged before a job lands, billing system can't deduct from committed bucket. Add to ticket.

jess: Ok closing loop for now. If the canary reduces on-demand hours in the 00:30-03:10 window simulation, we declare success and push a short-term policy change. Otherwise we'll evaluate capacity commit increases for Q2. :white_check_mark:
